narrative.overview: Tellura is structured as a mission-control instrument for high-dimensional planetary observations. Built for researchers, geoscientists, and the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, the interface prioritizes mathematical truth over decorative embellishment.
keyCharacteristics: Observational Rigor: Confidence intervals and FDR bounds on all data
Deep Space Ground: #0B1120 canvas paired with #2563EB Signal Blue
Dual-State Fidelity: Dedicated adaptive assets for Dark and Light modes
Sub-Second Responsiveness: Native Web Workers and Canvas rendering

rules.name: The Rarity of Signal Rule
rules.body: Signal Blue and trend colors are reserved exclusively for data vectors and verified telemetry.

rules.name: The Tabular Data Doctrine
rules.body: All numerical data, timestamps, coordinates, and statistical metrics must render in monospace or with tabular-nums.

rules.name: The Tonal Stack Rule
rules.body: Depth is created by lightening container backgrounds by 3-5% per layer, never by applying zero-offset drop shadow halos.

dos: Do format all scientific uncertainty bounds with symmetric or asymmetric brackets: [+0.12, +0.34].
Do use exponential easing (ease-out) for micro-interactions and modal entrances.
Do provide clear keyboard focus outlines on every interactive button, tab, and slider.
Do preserve the official Tellura Primary Horizontal Lockup image in headers and footers.
donts: Don't use cartoonish bounce or elastic easing (animate-bounce).
Don't use decorative gradient text that compromises readability.
Don't hardcode raw gray on colored surfaces; derive tints from the surface or foreground hue.
Don't truncate p-values or confidence levels to arbitrary whole numbers.
